## The durations package

`parse_duration(text: str) -> int` turns a duration into seconds. Plain
durations are one or more `<number><unit>` parts, in any order, with the
units `s`, `m`, `h` and `d`; case and surrounding spaces are ignored.

```python
>>> from durations import parse_duration
>>> parse_duration("1h30m")
5400
```

ISO 8601 durations such as `PT1H30M` or `P2DT4H` work too: they start with
`P`, their parts are in order (`PnYnMnDTnHnMnS`, or weeks alone as `PnW`),
a year counts as 365 days and a month as 30 days, and anything else raises
`ValueError`.

```python
>>> parse_duration("P2DT4H")
187200
```

The same parser runs from the command line: one number per line, and input
it cannot parse exits with status 2.

```bash
$ python3 -m durations 1h30m P2DT4H
5400
187200
```
```
